A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EasyRec by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original zero-shot recommendation experiments, collaborative-filtering comparisons, training-objective and profile-diversification analyses, and a preference-shift case study.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds experiments involving AlphaRec integration, LLMRank, alternative profile generators and recommendation diversity.

M1.justification: The profiling, RoBERTa encoder, CLS/MLP representation, contrastive-plus-MLM training, profile diversification and cosine-ranking pipeline are retained. v4 newly documents rationale prompting within the existing profiling step; this does not establish an actual procedural change. The written loss correction is assessed under T1.

E1.justification: The six Amazon training domains and Sports, Steam and Yelp evaluation datasets are retained. Appendix D adds a distinct profile-input scenario: evaluating EasyRec-Large on Sports profiles generated by DeepSeek-V3 instead of GPT-3.5. No new dataset domain or language is evaluated.

E2.justification: v4 adds LLMRank implemented with GPT-4o-mini as a zero-shot comparator in Appendix C/Table 6. Appendix A.3/Table 5 also compares AlphaRec+EasyRec against LightGCN; AlphaRec is evaluated as an EasyRec integration, not a standalone baseline. The comparator sets in the retained main experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces a separate ranking protocol with one ground-truth item and 19 negatives per user, reporting Recall@5/@10 and inference time alongside the retained all-rank evaluation. Appendix F.5 introduces ILD@5/@10/@20 for recommendation diversity. The stated Amazon rating filter also changes from greater than 3 to at least 3, although unchanged dataset counts and main results do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D/Table 7 adds robustness testing under a different profile-generating LLM, while Appendix F.5/Table 10 tests whether diversification improves recommendation-list diversity. These extend analysis to previously untested properties beyond v2's accuracy, augmentation-count and preference-shift investigations. The BPR-versus-contrastive analysis is retained in Appendix E rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run means for the retained Steam CF comparison and p < 0.05 markers in Table 3. The new AlphaRec comparison also reports averaged multiple runs, continuing the existing practice without specifying a new run count, increased budget, uncertainty measure or statistical test.

E6.justification: v4 adds results for AlphaRec integration, LLMRank comparison, generator robustness and recommendation diversity. For example, its 20-candidate comparison reports Recall@10 of 0.8078 for EasyRec versus 0.7822 for LLMRank; this is not a version-to-version performance gain. Table 3 is numerically identical, and retained CF scores match, but CF Recall@5/NDCG@5 entries disappear. The relocated objective ablation changes contrastive Sports Recall@10 from 0.0395 to 0.0396.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 11 places an erroneous minus sign before the positive exponential sum in the contrastive-loss denominator, making the logarithm's argument negative. v4 Equation 10 removes that sign. This corrects the mathematical expression; the remaining definitions and equations are essentially retained, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: aligning textual semantics with collaborative signals, cross-dataset zero-shot recommendation, plug-and-play CF enhancement and adaptation through profile updates. The added experiments support these contributions without substantially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v4 expands v2's brief multimodal future-work suggestion into an explicit limitation explaining what text-only inputs miss. Appendix D newly attributes generator robustness to diverse training texts and joint optimization across datasets. The zero-shot discussion also deemphasizes v2's explicit no-prior-interaction language in favor of generalization to unseen user/item sets.

D1.justification: v4 adds rationale-prompting details and identifies the LLMs used in its new experiments. However, it removes v2's maximum-five-item sampling specification for user profiling and explicit augmented-profile counts, and replaces separate input/output token counts with totals. Most training hyperparameters, checkpoint identifiers and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds discussion and references involving LLMRank, DeepSeek-V3, chain-of-thought prompting, DARec and recommendation diversity, while removing the SSLRec citation. Appendix A further distinguishes EasyRec's embedding role from integrated LLM-CF frameworks. The principal positioning against general-purpose text encoders and ID-dependent recommendation remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology, related work and conclusion undergo extensive sentence-level rewriting and condensation. The original Appendix A is reorganized into Appendices A–G, and the training-objective analysis moves out of the main evaluation section. Dedicated limitations and acknowledgments are added, alongside changed headings and citation style.

P2.justification: v4 changes the document template, typography, spacing, headers and placement of displays throughout. All seven figures remain, with caption and labeling edits. Four new tables are added; the objective table moves to the appendix, CF tables lose rank-5 columns, dataset statistics lose density, and the cost table combines token columns.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens the retained contribution through relevant generator-robustness and diversity checks, a direct LLMRank comparison, and correction of the invalid loss-denominator sign. The benefit is limited by reporting weaknesses: the ranker comparison covers only 20 candidates, Appendix D's GPT-3.5 scores are not clearly reconciled with Table 3, and the earlier five-item profiling cap is omitted. The additional evidence nevertheless provides a modest net improvement.
